results.title: Day 73/100: Data Augmentation Strategies for Robustness – Teaching Models to Expect the Unexpected | by Sebastian Buzdugan | Medium
results.content: # Day 73/100: Data Augmentation Strategies for Robustness – Teaching Models to Expect the Unexpected. Today, we turn to another critical technique for building resilient models: Data Augmentation. Let’s discover how to make your models stronger by expanding your data creatively and strategically. ## 🎯 Why Data Augmentation Matters. • Too narrow for real-world variability. • Models may overfit to the limited examples. • Fail on slightly different data. • Handle noisy, incomplete, or unseen inputs. ## 🔎 What Is Data Augmentation? Artificially creating new training examples by modifying existing data. • Rotating or flipping an image. • Adding noise to a signal. ## 🧠 Augmentation Techniques by Domain. • Color jittering, brightness/contrast changes. • CutMix, MixUp, and mosaic augmentations. • Synonym replacement (e.g., WordNet). • Back-translation (translate to another language and back). • Random deletion, swapping, or insertion. • Paraphrasing (e.g., with LLMs). • Noise injection (e.g., typos, misspellings). • SpecAugment: masking time and frequency bands. • Noise injection on continuous features. • SMOTE/ADASYN for imbalanced classes. • Generative models (e.g., GANs, VAEs) for synthetic data. ## 📊 Real-World Analogy – Training Like an Athlete. That’s data augmentation: preparing your model for the unexpected. ## 🛠 Tools for Data Augmentation. • Albumentations: Fast, flexible image augmentations. • Imgaug: Custom pipelines for vision tasks. • NLPaug: Augment text for NLP tasks. • TextAttack: NLP data augmentation and adversarial testing. • AudioAugment / torchaudio: Audio data transformations. • Snorkel: Programmatic labeling and augmentation for weak supervision. • AugLy: Multimodal augmentations (text, images, audio, video). ## 🔧 Best Practices for Data Augmentation. • Match augmentations to real-world scenarios your model will face. • Avoid unrealistic transformations that introduce noise (e.g., random color shifts in medical imaging). • Combine multiple augmentation types for rich variability. • Use probabilistic application (e.g., 50% chance of flipping an image). • Experiment with automated policies like RandAugment or AutoAugment. • Evaluate generalization improvements – augmentation shouldn’t just improve training metrics. • Too much augmentation = noise → poor learning. • Domain-specific caution: e.g., flipping text or code can corrupt meaning. • Computational overhead: More data = longer training. quantity: Some augmentations may hurt performance.

results.title: Generation Methods – Community Infrastructure to Strengthen AI for Audio Deepfake analysis (CISAAD) – UMBC
results.content: This page provides research work that explore generation of audio deepfakes and voice spoofing using methods including text-to-speech, and voice conversion. AdaSpeech is an adaptive text-to-speech (TTS) system designed to customize new voices efficiently and with high quality. Deep Voice 3 is a fully-convolutional, attention-based neural text-to-speech (TTS) system designed to match state-of-the-art naturalness in synthesized speech while training significantly faster than other models. DenoiSpeech is a text-to-speech (TTS) system designed to synthesize clean speech from noisy speech data. FastSpeech 2 is a non-autoregressive text-to-speech (TTS) model designed to synthesize speech faster and with higher quality than previous models. Glow-TTS is a flow-based generative model for parallel text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis that eliminates the need for external aligners by internally learning the alignment between text and the latent representation of speech. HiFi-GAN is a generative adversarial network for speech synthesis that achieves high-fidelity audio generation with efficient computational performance. LightSpeech is a lightweight and fast text-to-speech (TTS) model designed using neural architecture search (NAS) to achieve smaller memory usage and lower inference latency, suitable for deployment in resource-constrained devices like mobile phones and embedded systems. MelGAN is a non-autoregressive feed-forward convolutional architecture designed for audio waveform generation in a GAN setup, aimed at generating high-quality coherent waveforms for tasks such as speech synthesis and music domain translation. MelNet leverages time-frequency representations (spectrograms) instead of time-domain waveforms, using a highly expressive probabilistic model and a multiscale generation procedure to capture both local and global audio structures. A method that allows non-parallel many-to-many voice conversion (VC) using Star Generative Adversarial Networks (StarGAN). Tacotron 2 is a neural network architecture for speech synthesis directly from text. Novel voice conversion (VC) method using a Conditional Deep Hierarchical Variational Autoencoder (CDHVAE) to improve the naturalness and similarity of converted speech without requiring parallel corpora or text transcriptions. WaveGlow is a flow-based neural network designed to generate high-quality speech from mel-spectrograms efficiently and without auto-regression. #### WaveNet. WaveNet is a deep neural network for generating raw audio waveforms. It achieves state-of-the-art performance in text-to-speech (TTS) and can also model music and other audio modalities. ## I am interested in:.

results.title: [2310.03349] An Integrated Algorithm for Robust and Imperceptible Audio Adversarial Examples
results.content: [Submitted on 5 Oct 2023]. # Title:An Integrated Algorithm for Robust and Imperceptible Audio Adversarial Examples. Authors:Armin Ettenhofer, Jan-Philipp Schulze, Karla Pizzi. View a PDF of the paper titled An Integrated Algorithm for Robust and Imperceptible Audio Adversarial Examples, by Armin Ettenhofer and Jan-Philipp Schulze and Karla Pizzi. > Abstract:Audio adversarial examples are audio files that have been manipulated to fool an automatic speech recognition (ASR) system, while still sounding benign to a human listener. Most methods to generate such samples are based on a two-step algorithm: first, a viable adversarial audio file is produced, then, this is fine-tuned with respect to perceptibility and robustness. In this work, we present an integrated algorithm that uses psychoacoustic models and room impulse responses (RIR) in the generation step. We compare the different approaches in three experiments: in a simulated environment and in a realistic over-the-air scenario to evaluate the robustness, and in a human study to evaluate the perceptibility. Our algorithms considering psychoacoustics only or in addition to the robustness show an improvement in the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) as well as in the human perception study, at the cost of an increased word error rate (WER). **[v1]** Thu, 5 Oct 2023 06:59:09 UTC (1,496 KB). ## Access Paper:. results.title: Synthetic data generation using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs): Part 1 | by Daniel Huang | Data Science at Microsoft | Medium
results.content: # Synthetic data generation using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs): Part 1. GANs generate synthetic data that mimics real data. In this undertaking, researchers trained a specific GAN architecture called StyleGAN2 to generate synthetic images of human faces and display them on a website. GANs can generate several types of synthetic data, including image data, tabular data, and sound/speech data. GANs can also be used to generate tabular data, in an application that can help preserve privacy. In the paper “Data Synthesis based on Generative Adversarial Networks,” researchers propose a GAN-based method called table-GAN, which uses GANs to synthesize tabular data with similar statistical properties as the original tabular data while minimizing information leakage of the original data. GANs can also be used to generate sound data. GANs can be used as a tool to generate synthetic training datasets whenever data is scarce or expensive to obtain. For example, for datasets containing customer information, training Machine Learning models on GAN-generated datasets can protect customer privacy, as actual customer data is not exposed to any downstream Machine Learning models. GAN-generated images can achieve more diversity than can be obtained in simple transformations of the data. Augmenting a training dataset with GAN-generated data can allow a downstream model to both make better predictions as well as increase model robustness. As mentioned earlier, synthetic data from GANs can be used for downstream tasks (e.g., training a Machine Learning model) instead of using the original data, which protects the privacy of the original dataset. To achieve this goal, the generator of the GAN is also trained to defend against membership inference attacks while it maintains the quality of the synthetic data by sustaining a high level of performance with downstream Machine Learning tasks. The silver lining here, however, is that after spending the time and resources to train a GAN, actually generating the synthetic data is a quick and lightweight process. A related problem is when a GAN does not generate data with any diversity (which will also be covered in Part 2 of this article series). ## Synthetic data generation using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs): Part 2. ### Generative Adversarial Networks — GANs — employ a deep learning model to generate synthetic data that mimics real data….

results.title: What techniques are available for fine-tuning TTS models?
results.content: * What techniques are available for fine-tuning TTS models? # What techniques are available for fine-tuning TTS models? The following techniques are commonly used for fine-tuning text-to-speech (TTS) models to improve performance or adapt them to specific use cases:. 1. **Transfer Learning with Pre-trained Models**. Most modern TTS systems start with pre-trained models like Tacotron 2, FastSpeech, or VITS. Developers fine-tune these models on domain-specific data (e.g., medical terminology or regional accents) while keeping the base architecture intact. For example, retaining the encoder layers while retraining the decoder on custom audio-text pairs helps preserve linguistic understanding while adapting to new voice characteristics. This approach reduces data requirements compared to training from scratch. 2. **Data Augmentation and Multi-Speaker Adaptation**. Augmenting limited training data with techniques like pitch shifting, time stretching, and background noise addition improves model robustness. For multi-speaker TTS, methods like Global Style Tokens (GSTs) or speaker embedding layers enable a single model to mimic multiple voices. Meta-learning approaches like MAML can also help models quickly adapt to new speakers with minimal samples. * **Adversarial Training**: Using GANs to make synthesized speech indistinguishable from real recordings. * **Prosody Control**: Adding duration/pitch predictors to explicitly model speech rhythm and intonation. * **Knowledge Distillation**: Compressing large TTS models into lighter versions while preserving quality. Developers often combine these methods – for instance, fine-tuning a pre-trained FastSpeech 2 model with adversarial training and speaker embeddings to create a multi-voice system for audiobook generation. The choice depends on factors like available data, target hardware constraints, and specific quality requirements for the deployment environment.
